data.content_ref: inline:Priority-filtered attack relation: assign each argument a finite priority level from a configured total preorder, and retain an attack A→B only when priority(A) is strictly greater than priority(B), with committed roots given a unique top priority. This is a pure graph transformation before the grounded fixpoint, so determinism and polynomial cost are unchanged; reinstatement remains derived because the filtered graph is still an AF. Root validity is preserved because no retained attack targets a top-priority root. Weakness: priority is exogenous and cannot itself be challenged; if priorities are learned or contested, the semantics silently depends on an unadjudicated input.
